0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 -August 1965, after the draft finalized by the Fruits and Vegetables Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Canned peas are one of the most important processed vegetables. There is ample scope for the development of external as well as the internal trade. It is, however, necessary to ensure the quality of the product, if the demand is to be maintained and further developed. In order to ensure proper quality, it is necessary to have strict qualit! control based on specifications. It was, therefore, found necessary to formulate an Indian Standard specification for this product. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Rules framed thereunder, and also the Fruit Products Order, 1955. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wheiever applicable. 0.4 In this standard the trade designations and the trade sizes, along with the converted metric values, of the containers as at present being used within the country have been specified. These dimensions would be revised when an Indian Standard on open top sanitary cans is published. 0.5 This standard contains clauses which call for an agreement the purchaser and the vendor at the time of placing orders. vant clauses are listed below: a) Sizes and capacities h) Packing (see 6.1.3). of cans (see 6.1.2), and between The rele-

5. REQUIREMENTS shall be prepared and 5.1 Hygienic Requirements - The material handled under strict hygienic conditions by persons free from contagious and infectious diseases and only in premises maintained in a thoroughly clean and hygienic condition and having adequate and safe 4

IS: 3245 - 1965 watcxr supply and duly approved and licensed by the public health authorities concerned. All workers shall use clean, white, washed clothing (see IS: 2491-1963*). N eccssary precautions shall be taken to prevent incitltntal contamination of the product from soiled equipment or fi-elm personnel suffering from injuries. 5.1.1 .ill equipment coming in contact with raw materials or prodiic`ts in the tour-st' of manufacture shall be kept clean. An ample s~ipplv of steam ant1 Lvater, hose, brushes and other equipment necessar\. fol- proper- cleaning of machinery and equipment shall be available. The ecluipmcnt may be sterilized bv immersion in, or swabbing with, hypochlorite or other suitable chlorine solution. 5.2 General 1"~s at the tcristic5. - Canned peas shall be prepared from tender, fresh garden proper stage of maturity and of similar varietal charac-

5.3 Freedom from Preservatives, Artificial Colouring Matter and Flavouring Agents - The material shall be free from preservatives and artificial Aavouring agents. Permitted colours and mint leaves for fla\orrring may be used. 5.4 Requirements for Covering Brine - The covering brine chall be clear. The only substances that ma.y be added to the covering brine a~ edible common salt (sodium chloride), with or without a small quantity of sucrose, and citric or tartaric acid not exceeding 0.1 perctnt of the packing medium. 5.5 Requirements for the Finished Product-The can on opening shall display the following characteristics contents : of the

Grtrdc 1 -The canned peas shall possess a good, characteristic and practically uniform colour; shall be practically uniform in size; shall be practically free from defects; shall be practically free from *loose skins and splits; shall possess a good characteristic texture and normal flavour; and shall be of such quality with respect to clarity of covering liquor as to score not less than 85 points.
Grade 2 -The canned peas shall possess a characteristic and reasonably uniform colour; shall be reasonably uniform in size; shall free from loose be reasonably free from defects; shall be reasonably reasonably good skins and splits ; shall possess a characteristic texture and normal IIavour; and shall be of such quality with respect to clarity of covering liquor as to score not less than 75 points.

Grade 1 -The units shall possess a good, practically uniform colour, characteristic of peas of the proper maturity, which means that the colour shall be pale green to green; shall be practically free from any discolouration due to improper handling or processmg or other causes. Uneven distribution of pigments and change in colour normally associated with proper processing shall not be considered as defects. Grade 2 -The units shall possess a good, reasonably uniform colour, characteristic of peas of the right stage of maturity, which means that the colour shall be, pale green to green; shall be reasonably free from any discolouration due to improper handling or processing or other causes. Uneven distribution of pigments normally associated with proper processing shall not be considered as defects. 5.5.2 Texture and Uniformity of Size

Grade 1 -The units shall possess a practically tender texture, which means that the units shall be just fir-m but not hard and shall be characteristic of the peas which are of the proper stage of maturity. The units shall be practically uniform in size. Grade 2 - The units shall possess a reasonably tender texture, which means that the skins of not more than 5 percent by count of the peas shall be ruptured and the units shall be reasonably firm, but not hard. The peas shall normally be not starchy and over mature and the units shall be reasonably uniform in size. 5.5.3 Taste and Flavour and flavour characteristic units shall be completely

Grade 1 - The units shall possess taste of tender peas and the variety used. The 6

IS: 3245 - 1965 devoid of any sulphide odour, objectionable or off taste, smell sourness, off-taste and staleness. or odour, such as

Grade 2 `- The units shall possess taste and flavour characteristic of tender peas and the variety used. The units shall be devoid of any objectionable or off-taste, smell or odour, such as sulphide odour, sourness, off-taste and staleness. 5.5.4 Absence of Defects

Grade 1 -The units shall be practically free from defects, which means that there shall be present no extraneous vegetable material, not more than 5 percent by count of broken peas, not more than one percent by count of spotted or otherwise discolonred peas. The covering brine shall be practically clear, practically free from cloudiness, blackening or thickening and practically free from sediment. Grade 2 -The units shall be reasonably free from defects, which means that there shall be present extraneous vegetable material not more than 0.25 percent of the drained weight of peas, not more than 10 percent by count of broken peas, not more than 2 percent by count of spotted or otherwise discoloured peas. The covering brine shall be reasonably clear, which means that the liquor may be slightly cloudy and may possess a small quantity of sediment. 5.5.5 The material in Table 1. shall also conform to the requirements prescribed

PROCEDURE

A-2.1 Panel of Judges --~Judging ior grading the product shall lx done bv a panel of threr: ko five judges. All thr, judges constitutin? ;I panel shall be conversant lvith the factors ,governing tlrtx cjualit~- of The cans shall be opened and the contents poured tlie jxoduct. .iepar-ately into \vhitc par-celain flat trays. Each judge shall independc,ntlv r~snminc the contents fr-om each of the cans and assign scores for rliffrrent characteristics. A-2.1 .l `he jrrtlges shall consider the follopving characteristics: colour, texture and uniformity of size, taste and ,flavour, and absence of tlefrct5. A-2.2 System of Scoring -- The variations within each factor are so ticscribed that the scores may be ascertained for- each factor and esj)resstsd numerically. The relative importance of each factor has been expressed numerically on a scale of 100. Each judge shall give a score by the method described in Table 3 and for the individual factors, record his obserl-ations in the Score Sheet for Individual Judge (see P 13). A-2.2.1 The scores as number of points given on tire score sheet by the judges for the contents of each can for the four factors shall be recorded in a tabular form in the Score Card (SW P 1.5) and the average score calculated for each factor with overall average for each can entered in the appropriate columns of the Score Card aftcar complying with the conditions specified in A-2.3.1 and A-2.3.2. A-2.3 Ascertaining the Grade

A-2.3.1 Agrcellle?gf Ammg Judges - To ascertain the consistency of judgement among the judges, the total score assigned by each of them for the contents of the same can shall be caiculated by adding LIP tht~ scores for the 1YLJiOLIS individual characteristics. If the difference betwcen the maximum and the minimum of the total score so obtainecl does not exceed (Ii+Sj, where K is the number of judges, the scoring shall be deemed as consistent for the can under consideration. If the difference exceeds (K+S), the most outlying scar-e, that is, the one vvhich is far-thest from its immediate neighbour (the scores being arranged in one order), shall be discarded and the consistency among the remaining judges examined. is thus established (A-2.3.1), the A-2.3.2 When the consistency o\.erajl average scores given by the judges, whose scoring has been found to be consistent, shall be calculated for each can.
